# CASA requirement register

Source: [App Defense Alliance CASA Specification v2.1.1 (2026-06-03)](https://github.com/appdefensealliance/ASA-WG/blob/main/CASA/CASA%20Specification.md). Test procedures: [CASA Test Guide](https://github.com/appdefensealliance/ASA-WG/blob/main/CASA/CASA%20Test%20Guide.md).

Every audit item is checked on every commit by `scripts/verify.sh`:
- **verified**: the cited tests, lint rules and tools must exist and pass.
- **n/a**: if code matching a reopen pattern appears, the gate fails until the item is re-assessed.
- **pending**: work still owed. Allowed during development, but `CASA_STRICT=1` (release CI) fails.

✅ verified: **18** · ➖ n/a: **20** · ⏳ pending: **17**

## 2 Session Management

| ID | Requirement | Status | Evidence / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2.1.1 | Passwords, session tokens and API keys are not exposed in URL parameters | ✅ verified | `lint:secret-in-url`<br>`lint:oauth-implicit-flow` |
| 2.2.1 | Users can log out; logout or expiry invalidates all stateful session tokens, including refresh tokens | ⏳ pending | Sessions do not exist yet. Build them with the OAuth login: server-side session table, a logout endpoint that deletes the row, and idle/absolute expiry. |
| 2.2.2 | Other sessions can be terminated after a password change or reset | ➖ n/a | The app has no passwords; credential changes happen at Google. Revisit if local accounts are added. |
| 2.2.3 | Non-revocable stateless authentication tokens expire within 24 hours | ⏳ pending | Session design pending. Prefer opaque, revocable server-side sessions; any JWT must have exp <= 24h. |
| 2.3.1 | Cookie-based session tokens have the Secure attribute | ⏳ pending | `lint:cookie-flags`<br>No session cookie yet. lint:cookie-flags already rejects any cookie built without secure(true), http_only(true) and same_site. |
| 2.3.2 | Cookie-based session tokens have the HttpOnly attribute | ⏳ pending | `lint:cookie-flags`<br>No session cookie yet. lint:cookie-flags already enforces http_only(true). |
| 2.3.3 | Session tokens are used rather than static API secrets and keys | ⏳ pending | Authentication not built. Use per-user session tokens; do not add static shared API keys for clients. |
| 2.3.4 | Stateless session tokens are protected against tampering, replay, null cipher and key substitution | ⏳ pending | Session design pending. If stateless tokens are chosen, pin the algorithm, reject alg=none and validate iss/aud/exp. |
| 2.4.1 | A full valid session or re-authentication is required before sensitive transactions or account changes | ⏳ pending | Authentication not built. All state-changing endpoints must require a valid session. |

## 3 Access Control

| ID | Requirement | Status | Evidence / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1.1 | Least-privilege access control rules are enforced on a trusted service layer | ⏳ pending | BLOCKER: /api/notes is unauthenticated. Any client can list, read and delete every note. Add OAuth sessions, a notes.owner_id column, and scope every query to the session user. |
| 3.1.2 | User and data attributes used by access controls cannot be manipulated by end users | ✅ verified | `lint:permissive-deserialize`<br>`test:unknown_fields_are_rejected`<br>Every request body struct uses deny_unknown_fields, so server-controlled fields such as id, created_at and (later) owner_id cannot be mass-assigned. |
| 3.1.3 | Access controls fail securely, including when an exception occurs | ⏳ pending | `test:missing_limiter_fails_closed`<br>`test:internal_errors_do_not_leak_details`<br>No access control layer yet. Existing controls fail closed (missing limiter returns 500; internal errors are masked). Extend this to the auth middleware. |
| 3.1.4 | Sensitive resources are protected against IDOR on create, read, update and delete | ⏳ pending | BLOCKER: GET/DELETE /api/notes/{id} perform no ownership check. Fix together with 3.1.1. |
| 3.1.5 | Strong anti-CSRF protects authenticated functionality; anti-automation or anti-CSRF protects unauthenticated functionality | ✅ verified | `test:cross_site_form_post_is_rejected`<br>`test:rate_limit_returns_429_after_burst`<br>`lint:cors-wildcard`<br>State-changing endpoints accept only application/json, which a cross-site form cannot send without a CORS preflight, and no CORS is granted. | 3.1.6 | Directory browsing is disabled | ✅ verified | `lint:directory-listing`<br>`test:unknown_route_is_json_404` |
| 3.2.1 | Only secure OAuth 2.0 flows (Authorization Code, with PKCE) are used; implicit and password grants are not | ⏳ pending | `lint:oauth-implicit-flow`<br>Google OAuth not built yet. lint:oauth-implicit-flow already rejects response_type=token and grant_type=password. |
| 3.2.2 | redirect_uri and state are validated during OAuth authorization | ⏳ pending | Google OAuth not built yet. Use a fixed, registered redirect_uri; generate a random state, bind it to the pre-auth session and compare it on callback. |
| 3.3.1 | Application administrative interfaces use multi-factor authentication | ➖ n/a | The application exposes no administrative interface. |
